ri.purpose: Enables the resolution-of-the-identity (RI) approximation for the Coulomb (J) term, which fits two-electron integrals to an auxiliary basis to speed up DFT/HF SCF calculations. The manual notes the introduced error is very small and that RI is generally recommended for large systems. Turning RI on uses the Split-RI-J variant by default.
ri.pairs_with: a Coulomb fitting (/J) auxiliary basis; Split-RI-J is its default companion.
ri.defaults: RI-J is the default for non-hybrid DFT; Split-RI-J is the default when RI is enabled (RI.txt 2.8.1/2.8.2).
ri.typical_use: DFT and HF calculations on large systems where exact Coulomb integrals dominate cost.

rijcosx.purpose: Combines the Split-RI-J approximation for the Coulomb term with the chain-of-spheres (COSX) numerical treatment of exchange, accelerating Hartree-Fock and hybrid DFT. It needs a Coulomb fitting basis and adds a separate, usually much smaller, integration grid. Since ORCA 5 it is the standard default for hybrid DFT but is not turned on for HF automatically.
rijcosx.requires: a Coulomb fitting (/J) auxiliary basis (e.g. def2/J); a COSX integration grid.
rijcosx.pairs_with: a /J auxiliary basis, COSX grid settings, def2/J; NOCOSX disables the COSX part.
rijcosx.defaults: Default for hybrid DFT since ORCA 5; not on by default for HF (RI.txt 2.8.4).
rijcosx.typical_use: Default hybrid DFT for single points, gradients, frequencies and properties across system sizes, with near-linear scaling.
rijcosx.literature: manual cites references [119] and [120] for the COSX approximation.

rijk.purpose: Uses the RI approximation for both the Coulomb (J) and exchange (K) terms (full RI-JK), giving large speedups for Hartree-Fock and hybrid DFT. It requires an auxiliary fitting basis that can represent both the J and K integrals. The same approximation is reused in CP-SCF when active.
rijk.requires: an auxiliary fitting basis for both J and K.
rijk.excludes: fully analytical J and K evaluation in the SCF.
rijk.pairs_with: a fitting basis for (J) and (K); propagates into CP-SCF when active.
rijk.defaults: Not a default; must be requested. The manual notes RI-K is not especially efficient for response terms.
rijk.typical_use: Large HF and hybrid DFT single points, gradients and properties where RI-JK is affordable and accurate exchange is wanted.
rijk.literature: manual cites references [111],[112] for the RI-JK method.

rijksinglesfock.purpose: Documented in the ORCA 6.1.1 manual (see manual page). Semantics reconciled with the parser verdict (accepted).

rijonx.purpose: Applies the RI approximation to the Coulomb (J) term only and keeps the standard treatment for exchange, aiming for near-linear scaling of the exchange term on large molecules. It is intended for Hartree-Fock and hybrid DFT calculations.
rijonx.excludes: RI treatment of the exchange term.
rijonx.pairs_with: a Coulomb fitting basis; alternatives to full RI-JK for hybrid methods.
rijonx.defaults: RIJONX applies RI to Coulomb and standard treatment to exchange (RI.txt 2.8.3).
rijonx.typical_use: HF and hybrid DFT on larger systems where full RI-JK is not needed but efficiency of the Coulomb term matters.
rijonx.literature: the manual cites RI references in the RI section.
